prompt:
Scene:
Create a square standalone support image for Skinline Rarity Variant Suite. Build a profile-card crop emphasizing face recognition and rarity polish with a clear focal hierarchy and a finished professional surface. Use premium stylized key-art lighting, clean atmosphere, and enough negative space for campaign reuse. The frame should feel self-contained and polished, with enough structure to explain the system even without the reference series, yet still obviously belonging to the same theme and production world.

Subject:
Show the same original arena heroine with copper-brown skin, a sharp oval face, a silver undercut braid, amber eyes, and a compact athletic silhouette with a teal tactical mantle in a way that emphasizes the intended support surface. Keep the same character identity stable across pose and crop changes. Even though this image is independent, the viewer should still recognize the same universe, same commercial logic, and same production intent as the core package.

Important details:
Lock face, hair base, body proportions, costume logic, and palette with game-marketing polish. Preserve the broader theme language through color, framing, material choices, and modular composition. Use clean panel rhythm, premium asset presentation, and believable detail density. The image should work equally well as a gallery study, research reference, and mock production deliverable.

Use case:
Skinline Rarity Variant Suite single study 8/9, exploring profile card crop as a support surface.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no extra characters, no brand marks, no off-model face, no random colorway outside the chosen tier logic, no visual noise that obscures the main surface, no accidental brand resemblance.
